title: His father's guitar, the Werleins, and carrying the bass
summary: His father played straight guitar; Loyacano recalls neighbourhood trios and how the bass was lugged to jobs, and playing along with a player piano.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: mother and father play instruments? My father did.

What did he play? He played guitar. He did. Now, was he good? Well, I guess you'd call him good for those days. But your memory of his playing was he was all right? Oh, yes. He played the right key and everything. I mean, he didn't interpose any chords and stuff like they do today. It's all advanced. Straight stuff. Yes, he played only straight. They used to be fellas, I don't know whether you ever heard of the Werleins. Sure. Did you? George Werlein? Yeah. Jack Werlein? Yeah. Julie Oates? No, I don't remember. Oh, you never heard of him? Well, they had a three-piece band too. Bud used to play with them. Up in the Irish Channel? No, they lived on Gainey Street, Gainey near Constance, between Constance and Magazine. Oh, and I was just a kid then. Whenever I played any job, somebody usually had to carry the bass. Well, when you started playing the bass
as a kid, how'd you do about lugging that thing around? Well, I didn't carry it.

What happened? Usually, one fella'd carried a box, a soap box. Remember those wooden boxes, milk boxes, magnolia milk and all that? Well, he'd carry that, then usually Bud would carry the bass. Because Bud, for being a guitar player, I'd carry his guitar. Was he huskier than you were? Oh, yeah. Bud was a big man. He weighed all of 185 pounds for 5'10".
Uh-huh. He was husky. Well, before you actually got good enough to play with those kids' bands, did you all just play in the neighborhood? Did you have a little band that would make up in the

neighborhood? Well, I tell you, we had an old-fashioned player piano. And we used to get my nephew to pump it. Well, she had a pump it pedal, do you remember that? Yeah. And Joe and Jack would get out their horns and I'd get the bass fiddle and we'd play along with the old-fashioned piano. My nephew would paddlet.
